How High-Altitude Lidar Is Helping Utilities Prioritize Risk and Resources

2026-08-05 Geo Week News LiDAR, airborne lidar, utility mapping, Woolpert, ZEUS, Southern California Edison, high-altitude, geospatial intelligence, risk assessment, power infrastructure
Read the source article

Quick summary

Woolpert and Southern California Edison demonstrate how high-definition, high-altitude airborne LiDAR (ZEUS) is being applied to support one of the utility industry's most technically complex challenges, helping prioritize risk and allocate resources for power infrastructure.

Key takeaways

  • Woolpert's high-definition, high-altitude airborne LiDAR capability, called ZEUS, is being deployed in an active utility project with Southern California Edison
  • The webinar previews a broader Geo Week 2027 conversation on applying advanced geospatial intelligence in the field
  • High-altitude LiDAR enables proactive, data-driven utility operations by mapping infrastructure and terrain at high resolution from aircraft
  • The approach helps utilities identify risk priorities and allocate resources more effectively for power line maintenance and hazard mitigation
  • Speakers include Nathan Hopper, PhD, Discipline Leader for Advanced Sensing and Processing at Woolpert, and a representative from Southern California Edison
